ACT ON THE PREVENTION OF INSOLVENCY AND STRUCTURAL IMPROVEMENT OF FISHERIES COOPERATIVES

CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS <Amended Mar. 17, 2010>

Article 1 (Purpose)
The purpose of this Act is to protect members, depositors, and other persons and to contribute to the sound development of cooperatives by prescribing matters concerning the prevention of insolvency of cooperatives established under the Fisheries Cooperatives Act and structural improvements, including mergers of cooperatives and the disposal of non-performing assets. <Amended Feb. 18, 2020>

Article 2 (Definitions)
The terms used in this Act are defined as follows: <Amended Mar. 23, 2013; Feb. 18, 2020>
1. The term "cooperative" means a district fisheries cooperative, fisheries cooperative by business type, or fisheries product processing cooperative established under the Fisheries Cooperatives Act (hereinafter referred to as the "Fisheries Cooperatives Act").
2. The term "Federation" means the National Federation of Fisheries Cooperatives established under the Fisheries Cooperatives Act.
3. The term "insolvent cooperative" means a cooperative designated under Article 4 that falls under any of the following items:
(a) A cooperative whose liabilities exceed its assets as a result of an evaluation of its management status, or a cooperative for which normal management is clearly expected to become difficult due to a major financial incident or the occurrence of non-performing loans. In such case, the method for evaluating management status and the standards for valuing and calculating liabilities and assets shall be prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries;
(b) A cooperative that has suspended payment of deposit claims, etc., or repayment of borrowings from the State, a public body, the Federation, or another financial institution;
(c) A cooperative that would have difficulty paying deposit claims, etc., or repaying borrowings without external financial assistance or borrowings.
4. The term "cooperative at risk of insolvency" means a cooperative designated under Article 4 whose financial condition falls below the standards prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries and that is therefore highly likely to become an insolvent cooperative.
5. The term "business" means business under Articles 60, 107, and 112 of the Fisheries Cooperatives Act and Articles 9 and 10 of the Addenda to the Act Partially Amending the Fisheries Cooperatives Act (Act No. 7311).
6. The term "deposits, etc." means any of the following; provided, receipts from the Government, local governments, and other persons prescribed by Presidential Decree may be excluded:
(a) Deposits and installment savings received by a cooperative in the course of its credit business;
(b) Mutual-aid premiums received by a cooperative or the Federation in the course of its mutual-aid business.
7. The term "depositors, etc." means persons holding claims for deposits, etc., against a cooperative or the Federation.
8. The term "claims for deposits, etc." means any of the following:
(a) Claims held by depositors, etc., against a cooperative for the principal and interest of deposits or installment savings or other agreed monetary payments;
(b) Claims held by depositors, etc., against a cooperative or the Federation under a mutual-aid contract for mutual-aid benefits or other agreed monetary payments.
9. The term "insured event" means either of the following:
(a) Suspension of payment of claims for deposits, etc. (hereinafter referred to as a "Type I insured event");
(b) Revocation of authorization to establish a cooperative, a resolution to dissolve it, or a declaration of bankruptcy (hereinafter referred to as a "Type II insured event").
10. The term "financial assistance" means any of the following assistance furnished by the management agency at the expense of the Fund to an insolvent cooperative or a cooperative at risk of insolvency (hereinafter collectively referred to as "distressed cooperatives"), or to a person seeking to take over a distressed cooperative or acquire its business under Article 6, for improvement of the financial structure of distressed cooperatives and other purposes:
(a) Contributions or purchases of assets;
(b) Guarantees or assumption of liabilities;
(c) Loans of funds.
11. The term "Fund" means the Mutual Finance Depositor Protection Fund established and operated within the Federation under Article 20.
12. The term "management agency" means the Federation managing the Fund under Article 22.
13. The term "Fund Management Committee" means the committee established within the management agency under Article 21 to deliberate and resolve matters concerning operation of the Fund.

Article 3 (Duties of the Federation)
① The Federation shall develop and improve systems for preventing insolvency among cooperatives.
② The Federation may establish a computerized insolvency-prevention system to facilitate the prevention of insolvency among cooperatives and to manage such prevention efficiently.

CHAPTER I-2 PREVENTION OF INSOLVENCY AMONG COOPERATIVES <Newly Inserted Feb. 18, 2020>

Article 3-2 (Evaluation of Management Risks)
① To prevent insolvency among cooperatives, the Federation shall evaluate management risks each month for cooperatives other than distressed cooperatives (hereinafter referred to as "normal cooperatives" in this Chapter).
② Taking into account the results of the management-risk evaluation under paragraph ①, the Federation shall determine a management-risk grade for each normal cooperative in accordance with standards prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries.
③ The Federation shall notify normal cooperatives of the results of the evaluation under paragraph ① and the grades determined under paragraph ②, and report them to the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries.
④ Matters necessary for standards, procedures, and methods of management-risk evaluations under paragraph ①, and procedures and methods for notification and reporting under paragraph ③, shall be prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries.

Article 3-3 (Designation of Cooperatives Subject to Management Control)
① The Minister of Oceans and Fisheries may designate a normal cooperative as a cooperative subject to management control if it falls under any of the following:
1. Its grade determined under Article 3-2 (2) satisfies the criteria prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries;
2. It is otherwise recognized, based on the management-risk evaluation under Article 3-2 (1), that its management risks are increasing rapidly due to a decline in its net capital ratio, a financial incident, the occurrence of non-performing loans, or similar circumstances.
② Where the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries designates a cooperative subject to management control under paragraph ①, the Minister shall notify that cooperative and the Federation.

Article 3-4 (Management of Cooperatives Subject to Management Control)
① The Minister of Oceans and Fisheries may require a cooperative designated under Article 3-3 (1) (hereinafter referred to as a "cooperative subject to management control") to submit a management improvement plan and, if the submitted plan is considered inadequate, may require it to be revised or supplemented.
② From among cooperatives subject to management control, the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries may require a cooperative meeting the standards prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries, including a cooperative likely to be designated as a distressed cooperative, to make all or some of the following corrections. In such case, the Minister may require the cooperative to submit an action plan addressing the required corrections:
1. Formulation of a plan to reduce expenses;
2. Re-examination of the business feasibility of new projects and new equity contributions;
3. Establishment of special allowances for bad debts;
4. Formulation of measures to improve standards for handling loans and deposits and applicable interest rates;
5. Formulation of measures to improve fund management;
6. Re-examination of the business feasibility of investments in fixed assets;
7. Formulation of a plan to maintain an appropriate level of inventory assets;
8. Formulation of a plan to increase equity capital;
9. Other measures equivalent to subparagraphs 1 through 8 and recognized as necessary to prevent insolvency.
③ The Minister of Oceans and Fisheries may examine quarterly the implementation of corrective requirements by a cooperative to which a corrective requirement was issued under paragraph ②.
④ The Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall notify a cooperative subject to a corrective requirement under paragraph ② of the termination of that requirement if any of the following applies:
1. The cooperative has fully implemented the corrections required under paragraph ②;
2. It is recognized that the corrections required under paragraph ② are no longer necessary due to improvements in fund management or other circumstances;
3. Its designation as a cooperative subject to management control has been revoked under Article 3-5 (2).
⑤ Matters necessary for submission of management improvement plans, procedures for corrective requirements, submission of action plans, and termination of corrective requirements, other than those prescribed in paragraphs ① through ④, shall be prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries.

Article 3-5 (Revocation of Designation as Cooperatives Subject to Management Control)
① When six months have elapsed from the designation of a cooperative subject to management control, the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall review, in light of the reports under Article 3-2 (3), whether the cooperative no longer falls under any subparagraph of Article 3-3 (1).
② If the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries determines as a result of the review under paragraph ① that the cooperative need no longer be managed as a cooperative subject to management control, the Minister shall revoke its designation.
③ Upon revoking a designation under paragraph ②, the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall notify the cooperative concerned and the Federation.

CHAPTER II MANAGEMENT OF AND ASSISTANCE TO DISTRESSED COOPERATIVES

Article 4 (Designation of Distressed Cooperatives)
① Where a cooperative falls under any item of Article 2, subparagraph 3, or is highly likely to become an insolvent cooperative under subparagraph 4 of that Article, the management agency shall request the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries to designate it as a distressed cooperative upon resolution by the Fund Management Committee; provided, no resolution of that Committee shall be required for a cooperative falling under Article 2, subparagraph 3 (b).
② Upon receipt of a request under paragraph ①, the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall designate the relevant cooperative as a distressed cooperative if the Minister considers it necessary to manage it as such, and shall notify the cooperative and the management agency.

Article 4-2 (Prompt Corrective Measures)
① The Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall recommend, require, or order any of the following measures (hereinafter referred to as "prompt corrective measures") with respect to a distressed cooperative or its executive officers and, when issuing an order, shall also order the submission of an implementation plan. In such case, the Minister shall notify the management agency of the recommendations, requirements, orders, and other matters concerning the prompt corrective measures. <Amended Mar. 23, 2013; Feb. 18, 2020>
1. Cautions or warnings against a cooperative, or cautions, warnings, reprimands, or reductions in remuneration against its executive officers and employees;
2. Reduction of contributed capital, increase of equity capital, disposal of held assets, or reduction of business offices or organizational units;
3. Prohibition on acquisition of risky assets or restriction on acceptance of deposits at abnormally high interest rates;
4. Suspension of duties of executive officers or appointment of an administrator to act on their behalf;
5. Suspension of all or part of business (hereinafter referred to as "suspension of business");
6. Merger;
7. Transfer of all or part of business (hereinafter referred to as "business transfer") or transfer of contracts relating to all or part of business (hereinafter referred to as "contract transfer");
8. Other measures equivalent to subparagraphs 1 through 7 and considered necessary to improve the financial soundness of a cooperative.
② In recommending, requiring, or ordering prompt corrective measures, the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall recommend or require measures for a cooperative at risk of insolvency or its executive officers according to the degree of risk, and shall order such measures for an insolvent cooperative or its executive officers. In such case, the Minister shall determine and publicly announce in advance the standards and details necessary for prompt corrective measures. <Amended Feb. 18, 2020>
③ Where a distressed cooperative temporarily fails to meet the standards referred to in the latter sentence of paragraph ②, but is expected to meet them within a short period or another equivalent reason exists, the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries may defer prompt corrective measures for a specified period. <Amended Mar. 23, 2013; Feb. 18, 2020>
④ In setting the standards under the latter sentence of paragraph ②, orders to suspend all business, transfer all business or contracts, or take equivalent measures likely to cause substantial property losses to distressed cooperatives or their members shall be permitted only where the relevant cooperative is insolvent or its financial condition falls so far below such standards that a significant risk of harm to sound credit order or the rights and interests of depositors, etc., is recognized. <Amended Feb. 18, 2020>
⑤ When a distressed cooperative resolves on a merger under paragraph ① 6, notwithstanding the proviso to Article 40 and Article 43 (2) of the Fisheries Cooperatives Act (including cases where those provisions apply mutatis mutandis under Article 108 or 113 thereof), the merger may be resolved upon with the attendance or votes of a majority of its members and the consent of a majority of the members attending or voting. The same shall apply when a cooperative merging with a distressed cooperative resolves on the merger. <Amended Feb. 18, 2020>
⑥ Paragraph ⑤ shall apply mutatis mutandis where a cooperative resolves on a business transfer or contract transfer under paragraph ① 7, or intends to acquire the business or receive a contract transfer. Where a cooperative has delegates, "members" shall be construed as "delegates", and "voting members" as "voting delegates".
⑦ Where a cooperative intends to hold a resolution of its general meeting or delegates' meeting, a vote of members, or other proceedings concerning a merger, business transfer, or contract transfer under paragraphs ⑤ and ⑥, the management agency shall inform its members or delegates in advance of the extent of the cooperative's insolvency and matters relevant to the resolution or vote, including measures relating to the merger, business transfer, or contract transfer.

Article 4-3 (Changes to Prompt Corrective Measures)
If a distressed cooperative falls under any of the following, the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries may modify prompt corrective measures and recommend, require, or order the modified measures. In such case, the Minister may hear the opinion of the management agency as necessary and may require that agency to investigate the cooperative's management condition or take measures prescribed by Presidential Decree, including a management diagnosis:
1. The cooperative has failed to complete recommended, required, or ordered prompt corrective measures within the prescribed period;
2. It is considered unlikely that the cooperative will be able to complete the recommended, required, or ordered measures.

Article 5 (Supporting Measures for Implementation of Prompt Corrective Measures)
① When recommending, requiring, or ordering a merger, business transfer, or contract transfer under Article 4-2 (1), the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries may designate another cooperative and recommend that it merge with, acquire the business of, or receive the transfer of contracts from the cooperative subject to such recommendation, requirement, or order. <Amended Mar. 23, 2013; Feb. 18, 2020>
② The management agency may propose the amount, terms, and other conditions of financial assistance to a cooperative recommended to effect a merger, business acquisition, or contract transfer under paragraph ①, on condition that the cooperative implements the recommendation.

Article 6 (Applications for Financial Assistance)
A person intending to take over a distressed cooperative by contract transfer or merger, or to acquire its business, may apply to the management agency for financial assistance.

Article 7 (Financial Assistance)
① The management agency may provide financial assistance pursuant to a resolution of the Fund Management Committee in any of the following cases:
1. An application for financial assistance has been received under Article 6;
2. Assistance is deemed necessary to facilitate a merger, business transfer, or contract transfer involving a distressed cooperative;
3. Improvement of the financial structure of a distressed cooperative is considered necessary to protect depositors, etc., and maintain stability in credit order.
② The management agency shall establish the standards, methods, terms, and other matters necessary for financial assistance under paragraph ① following a resolution of the Fund Management Committee. <Amended Feb. 18, 2020>

Article 8 (Principles of Financial Assistance)
① When providing financial assistance, the management agency shall require equitable sharing of losses by persons responsible for the insolvency of the cooperative receiving assistance.
② The management agency shall provide assistance on condition that the recipient cooperative undertakes its own structural-improvement efforts, and may distribute assistance in two or more installments.
③ Deleted. <Feb. 18, 2020>

Article 9 (Execution of Agreements for Management Normalization)
① To provide financial assistance to a cooperative, the management agency shall enter into an agreement for implementation of management normalization (hereinafter referred to as an "agreement") with that cooperative; provided, an agreement with a cooperative other than a distressed cooperative need not cover matters other than those under paragraph ② 3. <Amended Feb. 18, 2020>
② An agreement shall include the following matters concerning management normalization of the cooperative:
1. Target levels for standards of financial soundness, including the net capital ratio, prescribed by Presidential Decree;
2. Target levels for standards of profitability, including return on assets, prescribed by Presidential Decree;
3. Plans for the stable management and repayment of assisted funds, including deposits with the Federation;
4. Other matters prescribed by Presidential Decree as necessary to normalize management of the cooperative.
③ The management agency shall disclose the agreement through electronic media or other means; provided, this shall not apply to matters prescribed by Presidential Decree that could significantly affect management of the cooperative.
④ The management agency shall report performance in implementing an agreement when requested by the competent standing committee of the National Assembly.
⑤ Deleted. <Feb. 18, 2020>

Article 9-2 (Management of Cooperatives That Have Entered into Agreements)
① The management agency shall inspect the implementation of agreements and the status of management improvement of cooperatives that have entered into an agreement under Article 9 (1) not more than twice each year.
② If, as a result of inspection under paragraph ①, the management agency recognizes that the financial structure of a cooperative may deteriorate further or that improvement thereof is inadequate, it may provide necessary support, including management guidance.
③ If a cooperative falls under any of the following, the management agency may require the head of the cooperative to rectify the situation or may demand dismissal or suspension from duty of an executive officer or disciplinary action against an employee:
1. Failure to perform the agreement;
2. Preparation of a false report or false materials under Article 9 or the agreement, or negligent failure to submit them without good cause.
④ The management agency shall report to the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries the results of inspections and support under paragraphs ① and ②.

Article 9-3 (Revocation of Designation as Distressed Cooperatives)
① If the management agency recognizes that a distressed cooperative no longer falls under any item of Article 2, subparagraph 3, or is no longer highly likely to become insolvent under subparagraph 4 of that Article, it shall, upon resolution of the Fund Management Committee, request the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries to revoke the designation as a distressed cooperative or change the designation of an insolvent cooperative to that of a cooperative at risk of insolvency. In such case, the management agency may also request termination or modification of a recommendation, requirement, or order for prompt corrective measures applicable to that cooperative.
② Upon receiving a request under the former sentence of paragraph ①, the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall revoke or modify the designation according to the following distinctions, and shall notify the cooperative concerned and the management agency. The Minister shall also notify them whether a recommendation, requirement, or order for prompt corrective measures will be terminated or modified in response to a request under the latter sentence of paragraph ①:
1. Where there is no longer a need to manage the cooperative as a distressed cooperative: revocation of its designation as a distressed cooperative;
2. Where it is necessary to continue managing an insolvent cooperative as a cooperative at risk of insolvency: change of its designation to a cooperative at risk of insolvency.

Article 10 (Administrative Dispositions)
① If a distressed cooperative violates or fails to comply with a requirement or order under Article 4-2 (1), the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries may, after hearing the opinion of the Fund Management Committee, order the suspension of duties of its executive officers, appoint an administrator to act on their behalf, or recommend dismissal of the executive officers to the general meeting (or the delegates' meeting, for executive officers elected at a delegates' meeting or a cooperative head elected by the board of directors). In such case, notwithstanding Article 57 (2) of the Fisheries Cooperatives Act (including cases where it applies mutatis mutandis pursuant to Article 108 or 113 thereof), the resolution shall be adopted with the attendance of a majority of members or delegates and the consent of a majority of members or delegates present. <Amended Mar. 23, 2013; Feb. 18, 2020>
② If an insolvent cooperative falls under any of the following, the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries may, after hearing the opinion of the Fund Management Committee, take necessary administrative dispositions against the cooperative, including a decision to transfer contracts, an order suspending business for a specified period not exceeding six months, or revocation of authorization for its establishment; provided, in the case of subparagraph 1, where the failure to comply with the order is attributable to the outcome of a resolution of a general meeting or delegates' meeting or a vote of members under Article 4-2 (5) or (6), the Minister shall, before taking a disposition, provide the cooperative an opportunity to explain itself as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended Mar. 23, 2013; Feb. 18, 2020>
1. The cooperative fails to comply with or becomes unable to comply with an order under Article 4-2 (1);
2. Its liabilities substantially exceed its assets, making it difficult to comply with an order under Article 4-2 (1);
3. It is clearly recognized that a sudden deterioration in its financial position will make payment of deposit claims, etc., or repayment of borrowings difficult, thereby harming the rights and interests of depositors, etc., or credit order.
③ The Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall hold a hearing before revoking authorization for the establishment of a cooperative under paragraph ②. <Amended Mar. 23, 2013>
④ When deciding on a contract transfer under paragraph ②, the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall specify the scope and terms of contracts to be transferred and the cooperative receiving the transfer (hereinafter referred to as the "assuming cooperative") to the extent necessary and obtain its consent in advance. In such case, the management agency may submit opinions to the Minister concerning detailed procedures relating to the scope and terms of the transferred contracts and the consent of the assuming cooperative. <Amended Mar. 23, 2013; Feb. 18, 2020>
⑤ The Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall appoint an administrator under paragraph ① for a cooperative ordered to transfer contracts under paragraph ②. <Amended Mar. 23, 2013>
⑥ Article 4-2 (5) shall apply mutatis mutandis where the assuming cooperative under paragraph ④ intends to consent to matters concerning a contract transfer. For a cooperative having delegates, "members" shall be construed as "delegates". <Amended Feb. 18, 2020>
⑦ Notwithstanding Article 4-2 (6), the Fisheries Cooperatives Act, and the articles of association of the relevant insolvent cooperative, a decision to transfer contracts under paragraph ② shall not require a resolution of its general meeting (or its delegates' meeting where it operates such a meeting). <Amended Feb. 18, 2020>

Article 11 (Effect of Decisions on Contract Transfers)
① Where a contract transfer is decided under Article 10 (2), the assuming cooperative shall succeed, at the time the transfer is decided, to the rights and obligations of the insolvent cooperative under contracts relating to the business included in the decision.
② Where a contract transfer is decided under Article 10 (2), the insolvent cooperative and the assuming cooperative shall jointly and without delay publish a summary of the decision and notice of the contract transfer in at least two daily newspapers.
③ Upon public notice under paragraph ②, the assuming cooperative shall succeed on the same terms to legal relationships between the insolvent cooperative and creditors, debtors, persons providing real security, and other interested persons (hereinafter referred to as "interested persons") in connection with the contract transfer. In such case, interested persons may assert against the assuming cooperative any grounds arising between themselves and the insolvent cooperative before the public notice under paragraph ②.
④ Public notice under paragraph ② shall be deemed to satisfy the requirements for asserting against third parties an assignment of a nominative claim under Article 450 of the Civil Act. In such case, interested persons may assert against the assuming cooperative any grounds arising between themselves and the insolvent cooperative before the public notice.
⑤ Where a contract transfer is decided under Article 10 (2), the assuming cooperative shall acquire rights in real estate and other property for which registration or recording is required upon publication of the notice under paragraph ②.
⑥ When deciding on a contract transfer under Article 10 (2), the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall require the insolvent cooperative and the assuming cooperative to preserve and manage materials relating to the contract transfer and allow interested persons to inspect them. The standards and procedures necessary for preservation, management, and inspection shall be prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries. <Amended Mar. 23, 2013; Feb. 18, 2020>

Article 12 (Appointment and Duties of Administrators)
① An administrator appointed under Article 4-2 (1) 4 or Article 10 (1) or (5) shall, in accordance with the purpose of appointment, have authority to perform the duties of the relevant executive officers or to manage or dispose of the assets and liabilities of an insolvent cooperative to the extent related to the decision on contract transfer. <Amended Feb. 18, 2020>
② If the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries orders the suspension of all business or decides on a contract transfer for a cooperative under Article 4-2 (1) 5 or Article 10 (2) (excluding an order to suspend all business due to a temporary shortage of funds where normalization of management is considered certain), the Minister may appoint executive officers or employees of the Federation as administrators as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries; provided, if necessary for normalization of management of the cooperative or protection of general creditors, persons other than executive officers or employees of the Federation may be appointed as administrators. <Amended Mar. 23, 2013; Feb. 18, 2020>
③ The Minister of Oceans and Fisheries may issue orders necessary for the performance of duties to an administrator under paragraph ①. <Amended Mar. 23, 2013>
④ If considered necessary for smooth implementation of prompt corrective measures, the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries may dismiss an administrator under paragraph ①. <Amended Mar. 23, 2013>
⑤ Upon appointing an administrator under paragraph ①, the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall, without delay, notify the district court having jurisdiction over the location of the cooperative's principal office and request the registry office having jurisdiction over that location to register the appointment of the administrator. <Amended Mar. 23, 2013; Sep. 20, 2024>
⑥ Article 11 (1) of the Commercial Act and Articles 30 and 360 through 362 of the Debtor Rehabilitation and Bankruptcy Act shall apply mutatis mutandis to administrators. In such case, "manager" in the Commercial Act shall be construed as "administrator"; and "bankruptcy trustee" and "court" in the Debtor Rehabilitation and Bankruptcy Act shall be construed as "administrator" and "Minister of Oceans and Fisheries", respectively. <Amended Mar. 23, 2013>

Article 13 (Purchase of Claims for Deposits, etc.)
① Where the management agency has paid insurance benefits or made advance payments of some claims for deposits, etc., under Article 30 (1) or (2), it may, at the request of depositors, etc., purchase claims for deposits, etc., relating to the insured event, other than rights acquired by the management agency under Article 33.
② Where the management agency purchases claims for deposits, etc., under paragraph ①, it shall pay depositors, etc., an estimated amount of their value. If the amount recovered on the purchased claims after deducting incurred expenses exceeds the amount paid to depositors, etc., the excess amount shall be paid additionally to the depositors, etc., concerned.
③ Matters necessary for the purchase of claims for deposits, etc., other than those provided for in paragraphs ① and ②, shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 13-2 (Measures against Inability to Pay Deposits, etc.)
If the management agency so requests because of a risk of significant harm to the interests of members and depositors, etc., arising from a cooperative's potential bankruptcy or inability to pay deposits, etc., the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries may order restrictions on the acceptance of deposits, etc., and the extension of credit, suspension of payment of all or part of claims for deposits, etc., or other necessary measures.

Article 14 (Petition for Bankruptcy)
If the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries becomes aware that a cooperative is subject to grounds for bankruptcy under Article 306 of the Debtor Rehabilitation and Bankruptcy Act, the Minister may file a petition for bankruptcy notwithstanding Article 85 of the Fisheries Cooperatives Act. <Amended Mar. 23, 2013>

Article 15 (Liquidators or Bankruptcy Trustees)
① Where a cooperative is dissolved and the management agency is its largest creditor as prescribed by Presidential Decree, a person appointed by the management agency from among the executive officers and employees of the Federation following a resolution of the Fund Management Committee shall become the liquidator, notwithstanding Article 86 of the Fisheries Cooperatives Act.
② Where a cooperative goes bankrupt and the court appoints a bankruptcy trustee under Article 355 of the Debtor Rehabilitation and Bankruptcy Act, the management agency may, following a resolution of the Fund Management Committee, recommend one executive officer or employee of the Federation as the bankruptcy trustee.
③ Articles 17 through 23 of the Act on the Structural Improvement of the Financial Industry shall apply mutatis mutandis to the bankruptcy of cooperatives. In such case, "financial institution" shall be construed as "cooperative", and "institution participating in bankruptcy proceedings" as "management agency".

Article 16 (Management Agency's Right of Subrogated Set-off)
On behalf of depositors, etc., the management agency may set off the claims for deposits, etc., held by each depositor, etc., as of the date of public notice of commencement of payment of insurance benefits and related matters under Article 30 (3) (hereinafter referred to as the "insurance-payment notice date") (excluding claims for deposits, etc., pledged by depositors, etc., to the cooperative as security for another person) against the liabilities owed by each depositor, etc., to the cooperative (excluding guarantee obligations).

Article 17 (Requirement to Obtain Liability Insurance)
① The management agency may require a cooperative (limited to a cooperative meeting the standards prescribed by Presidential Decree, such as erosion of equity capital) to obtain insurance (including mutual aid under the Fisheries Cooperatives Act; hereinafter referred to as "insurance" in this Article) to cover loss of the cooperative's property resulting from breach of obligations or torts committed by its executive officers or employees.
② If a cooperative fails to comply with the requirement to obtain insurance under paragraph ①, the management agency may conclude an insurance contract on its behalf.
③ If a cooperative fails to bear the premiums and other costs of an insurance contract concluded under paragraph ②, the management agency may deduct such costs from the insurance premiums paid by the cooperative under Article 29 (1); in such case, the corresponding amount shall be deemed not paid as an insurance premium.
④ Matters necessary for the methods and procedures for requiring insurance or procuring insurance on behalf of a cooperative under paragraphs ① and ② shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 18 (Demands to Exercise Claims for Damages)
① Where any of the following applies, the management agency may require the distressed cooperative concerned to claim damages against executive officers or employees recognized as responsible for its insolvency or risk of insolvency, persons falling under any subparagraph of Article 401-2 (1) of the Commercial Act, or other third parties (hereinafter referred to as "persons related to insolvency"):
1. Financial assistance is decided upon or provided under Article 7;
2. Insurance benefits are paid or some claims for deposits, etc., are paid in advance under Article 30 (1) or (2).
② A demand by the management agency under paragraph ① shall be made in writing, stating the reasons, method of claim, and period for making the claim.
③ If a distressed cooperative fails to comply with a demand under paragraph ①, the management agency may immediately claim damages by subrogation on behalf of the cooperative.
④ Where a distressed cooperative pursues a claim for damages under paragraph ① through litigation, the management agency may intervene in the pending litigation in support of the cooperative. Articles 71 through 77 of the Civil Procedure Act shall apply mutatis mutandis in such case.
⑤ Where the management agency prevails in exercising a claim for damages by subrogation under paragraph ③, or participates in litigation under paragraph ④ at the request of a distressed cooperative, the expenses shall be borne by the distressed cooperative.
⑥ Where a distressed cooperative has entered bankruptcy, a claim for expenses not borne under paragraph ⑤ shall be deemed a claim against the bankruptcy estate.
⑦ The management agency may investigate the affairs and property of the liquidating corporation or bankruptcy estate of the distressed cooperative concerned, if necessary to demand claims for damages, exercise such claims by subrogation, or participate in litigation under paragraphs ① through ④. <Amended Feb. 18, 2020>
⑧ Paragraphs ① through ⑥ shall apply mutatis mutandis to a cooperative surviving a merger with a distressed cooperative. In such case, the management agency may request that cooperative to submit materials necessary for a claim for damages against persons related to insolvency or for participation in litigation, and the cooperative so requested shall comply unless there is a compelling reason not to do so.

Article 19 (Requests for Provision of Materials)
If necessary for a claim for damages or participation in litigation by the management agency against persons related to insolvency, the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries may request the heads of relevant central administrative agencies, local governments, or other public institutions prescribed by Presidential Decree (hereinafter referred to as "public institutions") to provide materials or information concerning the property of such persons, and the heads of public institutions receiving such requests shall comply unless there is a compelling reason not to do so. <Amended Mar. 23, 2013>

CHAPTER III MUTUAL FINANCE DEPOSITOR PROTECTION FUND

SECTION 1 ESTABLISHMENT OF THE MUTUAL FINANCE DEPOSITOR PROTECTION FUND AND FUND MANAGEMENT COMMITTEE

Article 20 (Establishment and Sources of Funds)
① The Mutual Finance Depositor Protection Fund shall be established and operated within the Federation to cope with situations in which cooperatives engaged in credit or mutual-aid business (including the Federation in the case of mutual-aid business; hereinafter the same shall apply) are unable to pay claims for deposits, etc., due to bankruptcy or other causes and to promote the sound development of cooperatives.
② The Fund shall be financed from the following sources: <Amended May 29, 2016>
1. Insurance premiums paid by cooperatives;
2. Contributions from the Government;
3. Contributions from the Federation;
4. Borrowings from the Government, the Bank of Korea established under the Bank of Korea Act, the Federation, the Suhyup Bank established under the Fisheries Cooperatives Act, or financial institutions;
5. Funds recovered from financial assistance provided to distressed cooperatives under Article 7;
6. Funds recovered on claims for deposits, etc., purchased or acquired by the management agency under Article 13 (1) or Article 33;
7. Funds raised by issuing bonds of the Mutual Finance Depositor Protection Fund (hereinafter referred to as "Fund bonds") under Article 27 (2);
8. Earnings from the operation of the Fund and other income.

Article 21 (Fund Management Committee)
① The management agency shall establish a Fund Management Committee to deliberate and resolve the following matters concerning the operation of the Fund: <Amended Mar. 23, 2013; Feb. 18, 2020>
1. Raising, operation, and management of the Fund;
2. Establishment of the target level of the Fund's reserves under Article 29-2 and payment of insurance benefits;
3. Designation and revocation of designation of distressed cooperatives, and assistance thereto;
4. Borrowings;
5. Issuance of Fund bonds;
6. Enactment, amendment, and repeal of regulations concerning the Fund;
7. Other matters requested by the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries or deemed necessary by the Fund Management Committee and submitted to its meetings.
② The Fund Management Committee shall consist of the following members, including one chairperson and one vice-chairperson. The president of the Federation shall be its chairperson, and the chairperson of the Cooperative Audit Committee under Article 143 of the Fisheries Cooperatives Act shall be its vice-chairperson. <Amended Mar. 23, 2013; Oct. 1, 2025>
1. One person commissioned by the president of the Federation from among the heads of cooperatives, excluding heads of insolvent cooperatives or cooperatives at risk of insolvency;
2. One person designated by the president of the Federation from among its executive officers and employees;
3. One person designated by the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries from among public officials under the Minister's jurisdiction;
4. One person designated by the Minister of Finance and Economy from among public officials under the Minister's jurisdiction;
4-2. One person designated by the Minister of Planning and Budget from among public officials under the Minister's jurisdiction;
5. One person designated by the Chairperson of the Financial Services Commission from among public officials under the Chairperson's jurisdiction;
6. Two persons with extensive knowledge and experience in fisheries and cooperatives commissioned by an organization related to fisheries designated by the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries (limited to nonprofit corporations established under Article 32 of the Civil Act);
7. Two persons with extensive knowledge and experience in cooperatives, finance, and accounting commissioned by the competent standing committee of the National Assembly;
8. One person with extensive knowledge and experience in finance and accounting commissioned by the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries.
③ The term of office of a member referred to in paragraph ② 1 or 6 through 8 shall be three years, and members may be reappointed.
④ Matters necessary for the operation of the Fund Management Committee, other than those prescribed in paragraphs ① through ③, shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

SECTION 2 MANAGEMENT AND OPERATION

Article 22 (Management Agency)
① The Federation shall be the management agency of the Fund.
② Upon request of the competent standing committee of the National Assembly, the management agency shall submit a report concerning operation of the Fund and other relevant matters.

Article 23 (Business of the Management Agency)
To achieve the purposes of this Act, the management agency shall perform the following business:
1. Demands to exercise claims for damages under Article 18 and related matters;
2. Collection of insurance premiums under Article 29;
3. Payment of insurance benefits under Article 30 and related matters;
4. Business entrusted or designated by the Government to protect depositors, etc.;
5. Business incidental to the business referred to in subparagraphs 1 through 4;
6. Other business concerning management of and assistance to distressed cooperatives under this Act.

Article 24 (Uses of the Fund)
The Fund may be used only for the following purposes: <Amended Feb. 18, 2020>
1. Financial assistance under Article 7;
2. Purchase of claims for deposits, etc., under Article 13 (1);
3. Repayment of principal and interest on borrowings and Fund bonds under Article 20 (2) 4 and 7;
4. Payment of insurance benefits under Article 30 (1) and (2) and related matters;
5. Other expenses necessary for the operation and management of the Fund.

Article 25 (Surplus Funds)
The management agency may operate surplus funds of the Fund by the following methods:
1. Purchase of national or public bonds or other securities designated by the Fund Management Committee;
2. Deposits with or short-term loans to financial institutions designated by the Fund Management Committee;
3. Other methods prescribed by the Fund Management Committee.

SECTION 3 FINANCE AND ACCOUNTING

Article 26 (Accounting of the Fund)
① The fiscal year of the Fund shall coincide with the fiscal year of the Government.
② The budget and settlement of accounts of the Fund shall be approved by the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries following a resolution of the Fund Management Committee. <Amended Mar. 23, 2013>
③ The accounts of the Fund and the Federation shall be kept separately, and the Fund shall maintain separate accounts for credit business and mutual-aid business.
④ Matters necessary for loans and transfers of funds between the accounts under paragraph ③, calculation of expenses, and other relevant matters shall be determined by the Fund Management Committee.

Article 27 (Borrowing Funds and Issuing Fund Bonds)
① The Government may guarantee repayment of the principal and interest of funds borrowed under Article 20 (2) 4.
② The management agency may issue Fund bonds at the expense of the Fund following a resolution of the Fund Management Committee. In such case, Article 156 (4) and (5) and Articles 157 through 160 of the Fisheries Cooperatives Act shall apply mutatis mutandis.
③ Matters necessary for the issuance and subscription of Fund bonds, other than those prescribed in paragraph ②, shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

CHAPTER IV DEPOSIT INSURANCE

Article 28 (Insurance Relationships)
An insurance relationship among the management agency, a cooperative, and depositors, etc., shall be established when depositors, etc., acquire claims for deposits, etc., against the cooperative.

Article 29 (Payment of Insurance Premiums)
① A cooperative shall pay insurance premiums on deposits, etc., to the Fund as prescribed by Presidential Decree. In such case, different premium rates may be applied to cooperatives in consideration of their management and financial condition, the amount of reserves in each account under Article 26 (3), and other factors.
② A cooperative that fails to pay premiums by the payment deadline shall pay the management agency the overdue charges prescribed by Presidential Decree in addition to the premiums.
③ A cooperative may not demand a refund of premiums paid under paragraph ①.
④ Matters necessary for the methods and timing of payment of insurance premiums under paragraph ① shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 29-2 (Establishment of Target Level of Fund Reserves)
① The management agency shall establish a target level of reserves of the Fund (hereinafter referred to as the "target level" in this Article) so that the Fund's reserves remain at an appropriate level.
② The target level shall be determined for each account under Article 26 (3), following a resolution of the Fund Management Committee and in consideration of the management and financial condition of cooperatives, within the limits that do not impede efficient operation of the mutual finance depositor protection system. The target level may be defined as a range with an upper and a lower limit.
③ The management agency shall periodically review the appropriateness of the target level, considering management conditions of cooperatives and stability of the mutual finance depositor protection system, and may reset the target level following a resolution of the Fund Management Committee when necessary.
④ Notwithstanding Article 29 (1), where the Fund's reserves reach the target level, the management agency shall reduce the insurance premiums payable by cooperatives as prescribed by Presidential Decree, taking account of the expected future income and expenditure of the Fund. Such a reduction shall be decided upon following a resolution of the Fund Management Committee.

Article 30 (Payment of Insurance Benefits)
① Where an insured event occurs at a cooperative, the management agency shall pay insurance benefits upon request of depositors, etc., of that cooperative as prescribed by Presidential Decree; provided, in the case of a Type I insured event, the management agency shall decide whether to pay insurance benefits following a resolution of the Fund Management Committee within two months from the date it receives notification under Article 32 (2).
② In the case of a Type I insured event, the management agency may, upon request of depositors, etc., make advance payment of part of their claims for deposits, etc., as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
③ The management agency shall give public notice of the commencement date, period, and method of payments under paragraph ① or ② and other necessary matters as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
④ Where a cooperative established by merger or surviving after merger continues the business of a cooperative extinguished by merger, the cooperative established by merger, the surviving cooperative, and the extinguished cooperative shall each be deemed to exist as an independent cooperative for the purposes of paragraph ① until one year after registration of the merger.
⑤ Where a Type II insured event occurs after a Type I insured event, the Type II insured event shall not be regarded as a separate insured event for the purposes of paragraph ①.
⑥ In paying insurance benefits under paragraph ①, the management agency may defer payment for a period not exceeding six months from the date of public notice of payment of insurance benefits under paragraph ③ with respect to amounts prescribed by Presidential Decree, including guarantee obligations of depositors, etc., to the cooperative concerned.
⑦ The right of depositors, etc., to claim insurance benefits under paragraph ① shall be extinguished by prescription if not exercised within five years from the commencement date of payments under paragraph ③.

Article 31 (Calculation of Insurance Benefits)
① Insurance benefits paid to depositors, etc., under Article 30 (1) shall be the amount obtained by subtracting the aggregate amount of liabilities (excluding guarantee obligations) owed by each depositor, etc., to the cooperative from the aggregate amount of claims for deposits, etc., held by that depositor, etc., as at the insurance-payment notice date.
② The benefits under paragraph ① shall not exceed the amount prescribed by Presidential Decree in consideration of the amount of protected deposits, etc., and other circumstances.
③ Where a depositor, etc., has received advance payments under Article 30 (2) (hereinafter referred to as "advance payments"), the insurance benefits shall equal the amount calculated under paragraphs ① and ② minus the advance payments.
④ Where advance payments made to a depositor, etc., exceed the insurance benefits calculated under paragraphs ① and ②, that depositor, etc., shall return the excess to the management agency. <Amended Feb. 18, 2020>

Article 32 (Notification of Insured Events)
① A cooperative shall notify the management agency without delay of the occurrence of an insured event.
② The Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall notify the management agency without delay if any of the following applies: <Amended Mar. 23, 2013; Feb. 18, 2020>
1. The Minister orders suspension of payment of claims for deposits, etc., of a cooperative, suspension of business or duties, or suspension of debt payments under Article 4-2 (1) 5, Article 10 (2), or Article 170 (3) or 172 (3) of the Fisheries Cooperatives Act;
2. The Minister revokes authorization for establishment of a cooperative or authorizes a resolution for its dissolution.

Article 33 (Acquisition of Claims for Deposits, etc.)
Where the management agency pays insurance benefits and advance payments under Article 30 (1) and (2), it shall acquire the rights of depositors, etc., against the cooperative concerned to the extent of the amounts paid.

CHAPTER V SUPERVISION, ETC.

Article 34 (Supervision)
① The Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall supervise the business of the management agency and may issue orders necessary for that purpose. <Amended Mar. 23, 2013>
② If deemed necessary for supervision under paragraph ①, the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries may require the management agency to report on its business, accounting, and property, and may have subordinate public officials inspect its business condition, books, documents, facilities, or other necessary articles. <Amended Mar. 23, 2013>
③ If deemed necessary for supervision under paragraph ①, the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries may request the Governor of the Financial Supervisory Service to inspect the management agency. <Amended Mar. 23, 2013>

Article 35 (Entrustment of Authority)
The Minister of Oceans and Fisheries may entrust part of the authority under this Act to the president of the Federation or the head of the management agency as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended Mar. 23, 2013>

CHAPTER VI PENALTY PROVISIONS <Amended Mar. 17, 2010>

Article 36 (Penalty Provisions)
An executive officer (excluding a non-executive officer), administrator, or liquidator of a cooperative who fails to implement procedures or measures necessary to comply with an order under Article 4-2 (1) shall be punished by imprisonment for not more than two years or a fine not exceeding 20 million won. <Amended Feb. 3, 2015; Feb. 18, 2020>

Article 37 (Penalty Provisions)
A person falling under any of the following shall be punished by imprisonment for not more than one year or a fine not exceeding 10 million won: <Amended Feb. 3, 2015>
1. A person who refuses, obstructs, or evades an investigation under Article 18 (7);
2. A person who fails to submit materials or submits false materials in violation of the latter sentence of Article 18 (8).

Article 38 (Joint Penal Provisions)
Where an executive officer, employee, administrator, or liquidator of a cooperative commits a violation under Article 36 or 37 in connection with the business of the cooperative, the cooperative shall also be subject to the fine prescribed in the relevant Article, in addition to punishment of the offender; provided, this shall not apply where the cooperative has not neglected reasonable care and supervision with regard to the relevant business to prevent the violation.

Article 39 (Administrative Fines)
① A cooperative falling under any of the following shall be subject to an administrative fine not exceeding 20 million won:
1. Failure to give public notice under Article 11 (2);
2. Failure to preserve and manage materials or make them available for inspection under Article 11 (6);
3. Failure to notify the management agency of an insured event under Article 32 (1).
② A head, executive director, administrator, or liquidator of a cooperative who violates Article 11 (2) or (6) shall be subject to an administrative fine not exceeding 10 million won.
③ A head, executive director, or administrator of a cooperative who violates Article 32 (1) shall be subject to an administrative fine not exceeding two million won.
④ Administrative fines under paragraphs ① through ③ shall be imposed and collected by the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended Mar. 23, 2013>
